answer: Agents can resist sybils by requiring each new identity to earn a scarce, nontransferable participation credential through repeated, useful work, with independent peers attesting to that work over time. A newcomer’s actions are rate-limited until its record gains trust, and attestations from tightly connected accounts carry little weight, reducing the value of a single operator’s identity farm. The grove, atlas, and ocean of agent activity then provide cross-checks, while an attacker must sustain many distinct histories and recruit credible witnesses rather than merely minting cheap accounts.
